questions.question: Which of the following dance form is related with Assam?

__
 
• Bihu is the famous dance form of Assam, a state located in northeastern India.
 
• It is an integral part of the Bihu festival, which is the most important festival in Assam and is celebrated to mark the agricultural cycle.
 
• Bihu is characterized by energetic movements, rhythmic footwork, and graceful hand gestures.
 
• The Bihu dance is performed by both men and women, usually in groups.
 
• It is accompanied by traditional Bihu music, which includes the use of instruments like the **dhol (a double-headed drum), pepa (a buffalo hornpipe), and taal (a cymbal).**
 
• The dancers wear colorful traditional attire, with women typically dressed in Mekhela Chador, a two-piece garment, and men wearing dhoti and kurta.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kalbeliya **is a famous dance form of** Rajasthan, a state in northwestern India.**

 
 
• It is primarily associated with the** Kalbeliya community, a nomadic tribe **known for their snake-charming skills and their distinctive dance style.
 
• The Kalbeliya dance is an integral part of their cultural expression and has gained recognition and popularity worldwide. **The Kalbeliya dance** is characterized by its graceful and rhythmic movements, which imitate the fluid and sinuous movements of a snake. 
 
 
 
• **Kathak is one of the major classical dance forms of India, originating from the northern region of the country, particularly in the states of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan.**
 
 
• It is a highly expressive dance form that combines rhythmic footwork, intricate hand gestures, facial expressions, and storytelling.
 
 
 
• **Bhangra is a lively and energetic dance form that originated in the Punjab region of India and Pakistan.**
 
 
• It is a traditional folk dance and music style that has become popular worldwide.
 
• Bhangra is associated with the harvest season and is often performed during festivals and celebrations.

questions.question: ______ is the largest producer of bauxite in the world.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 3**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** Australia** is the **world's largest producer of bauxite**, with production amounting to an estimated **100 million metric tons in 2022.**
 
• **Formation and Composition:** Bauxite is a sedimentary rock that is primarily composed of aluminum hydroxide minerals, iron oxides, and various impurities. It is formed through the weathering and erosion of rocks in tropical and subtropical areas, where high rainfall and prolonged exposure to moisture contribute to its development over millions of years.
 
• **Aluminum Ore:** Bauxite is the primary source of aluminum metal. It contains a significant amount of alumina (aluminum oxide), which is extracted from the bauxite ore through a refining process known as the Bayer process. Alumina is then further processed to obtain aluminum metal used in a wide range of industries, including transportation, construction, packaging, and electrical applications.
 
• **Global Reserves and Production: **Bauxite reserves are found in various countries around the world, with the largest deposits located in Australia, Guinea, Brazil, China, and India. These countries account for the majority of global bauxite production. The availability and accessibility of bauxite deposits, along with economic factors and environmental considerations, influence production levels in different regions.
 
• **Environmental Impact and Sustainability:** Bauxite mining and processing can have significant environmental impacts. The extraction of bauxite often involves clearing forests, disrupting ecosystems, and generating large amounts of waste, including red mud, which is a byproduct of the refining process. Sustainable mining practices, land rehabilitation efforts, and technological advancements are being pursued to mitigate these environmental concerns and promote responsible bauxite production.

questions.question: Who is the highest law officer in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attorney General for India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Attorney General (AG) of India

 
 
• This is a part of the Union Executive. AG is the highest law officer in the country.
 
• Article 76 of the Constitution provides for the office of AG of India.
 
• AG is appointed by the President on the advice of the government.
 
• S/he must be a person who is qualified to be appointed a judge of the Supreme Court, i.e. s/he must be a citizen of India and must have been a judge of some high court for five years or an advocate of some high court for ten years or an eminent jurist, in the opinion of the President.
 
• Term of the Office: Not fixed by the Constitution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vice President of India **

 
 
• The vice pres ident of India is the deputy to the head of state of the Republic of India, i.e. the president of India.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both Houses of Parliament, in accordance with the system of proportional Representation.
 
• Article 324 of the Constitution read with the Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections.
 
• The 14th and current vice president of India is Jagdeep Dhankar.
 
 

Thus, the Vice-Pres ident of India is elected by Members of Parliament

 
• **Chief Justice of India**

 
 
• The Chief Justice of India (CJI) is appointed by the President of India under clause (2) of Article 124 of the Constitution.
 
• 
 The chief justice is appointed by the president after consultation with such judges of the Supreme Court and high courts as he

 deems necessary.
 
 
• 
 The other judges are appointed by the president after consultation with the chief justice and such other judges of the Supreme Court and the high courts as he deems necessary.
 
 
• 
 Consultation with the chief justice is obligatory in the case of the appointment of a judge other than the Chief justice.
 
 
 
 
• **​Solicitor General of India**

 
• The Solicitor General of India is a** Legal advisor**.

 
 
• The Solicitor General of India is subordinate to the Attorney General of India.
 
• He himself assisted by several Additional Solicitor Generals of India.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. Salts of a strong acid and weak base are acidic with pH value less than 7.

II. When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of sodium chloride (called brine), it decomposes to form sodium oxide.
questions.solution:
Correct Answer **Only I**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The pH value of salts of strong acid and strong base is 7__.

 __
 
• The salts are from a strong acid and strong base that do not hydrolyze and the resulting salt pH will remain 7.
 
• The anion in the salt form's strong base does not attract the H+ from the water.
 
 
 
• Salt of a strong acid and a weak base is acidic with a pH value less than 7 because acid is strong which retains the pH value less than 7. ***Statement I is correct__***
 
• Salt of a weak acid and strong base is base with a pH value of more than 7 because the base is strong hence pH of the whole solution will be more than 7.
 
• Salt of a strong acid and strong base is neutral because both are strong and cancels strong effects of each other, the pH will be 7.

Statement II:(Incorrect)

 
• When electricity is passed through an aqueous solution of **sodium Chloride (brine),** it decomposes to form **NaOH + H₂ + CI₂.**
 
• **Brine** is a saturated solution of **NaCl (Sodium chloride).**
 
• Electrolytic decomposition of solution gives** Cl₂ (Chlorine)** at the **anode **and **H₂ (Hydrogen)** is formed at the** cathode and NaOH (Sodium hydroxide )** is formed near to the cathode.
 
• This process is known as **chor- alkali process.**

questions.question: Who among the following was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal for the majority of his/her life?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mother Teresa.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mother Teresa, officially known as Saint Teresa of Calcutta, was a Roman Catholic missionary who worked in Bengal, particularly in Kolkata (formerly known as Calcutta), for the majority of her life.
 
• She dedicated her life to serving the poor, sick, and marginalized people in Kolkata, establishing the Missionaries of Charity and receiving worldwide recognition for her humanitarian work.
 
• Mother Teresa, originally named Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu, was born on August 26, 1910, in Skopje, now North Macedonia.
 
• She joined the Sisters of Loreto at the age of 18 and moved to Ireland to train as a missionary.
 
• In 1929, Mother Teresa arrived in Kolkata (formerly Calcutta), India, where she taught at St. Mary's School for girls.
 
• During a train ride to Darjeeling in 1946, she experienced what she referred to as a "call within a call" from God to work among the poorest of the poor.
 
• In 1950, Mother Teresa founded the Missionaries of Charity, a Roman Catholic religious congregation dedicated to serving the destitute and dying.
 
• The Missionaries of Charity focused on providing care, shelter, and support to the sick, homeless, orphans, lepers, and individuals dying on the streets of Kolkata.
 
• Mother Teresa's selfless and dedicated service to the poor and marginalized garnered global attention, and the Missionaries of Charity expanded internationally.
 
• She received numerous awards and honors for her humanitarian work, including the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Who among the following won the Singapore Formula 1 Grand Prix 2022?
questions.solution:

• Charles Leclerc finished second, while Carlos Sainz Jr. finished third.
 
• Max Verstappen retired from the race with a mechanical problem.
 
• The race was held in wet conditions, making it a challenging one for the drivers.
 
• Perez started the race from pole position and led from start to finish.
 
• Leclerc made a late charge for the lead, but was unable to pass Perez.

• The races are held on purpose-built circuits and public roads around the world.
 
• The Formula One World Championship is the highest class of single-seater auto racing sanctioned by the FIA.
 
• The championship consists of a series of races held over a period of several months.
 
• The drivers and constructors with the most points at the end of the season are crowned champions.
 
• The first Formula One Grand Prix was held in 1950 at Silverstone Circuit in England.

questions.question: When did depressed classes get the reserved seats in provincial and central legislative councils, but they were to be voted in by General electorate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**September 1932**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Poona Pact: (1932)**

 
 
• **Poona Pact **was signed in the year **1932**.
 
• The reason for the Poona Pact was the **Communal Award of August 1932 which provided a separate electorate for depressed classes.**
 
• Poona pact signed between Dr B R Ambedkar and Gandhiji.
 
• **Poona pact was signed on September 24, 1932, at Yerwada Jail in Pune.**
 
• Madan Mohan Malaviya signed it on behalf of upper-caste Hindus and Gandhi.
 
• Ambedkar signed on behalf of depressed classes.
 
• The final outcome of the Poona pact was 147 electoral seats.
 
 
 
• Provisions of the Poona Pact: 
 
 
• Seats would be reserved for the ‘Depressed classes’ in the Provincial Councils.
 
• The number of seats reserved for the provinces depended on the strength of the provinces:
 
• Madras: 30; Punjab: 8; Bombay and Sindh: 15; Central Provinces: 20; Bihar and Orissa: 18; Bengal: 30; United Provinces: 20; and Assam: 7 (Total reserved: 148)
 
• In the Central Legislature, 19% of the seats would be reserved for the Depressed Classes.
 
• The members of the depressed classes who were eligible to vote would form an electoral college.
 
• This College would elect four candidates among the depressed classes on the basis of a single vote.
 
• That is, the candidates with the four highest numbers of votes would form the panel of four).
 
• Then, these four candidates would stand for election with the general candidates for election to the assembly.
 
• This time, the general electorate would vote. Thus, in effect, the depressed classes got a ‘double vote’ since they formed part of the general electorate also.

 This principle of ‘Joint electorate and reserved seats’ was to be followed in the Central Assembly too.
 
• It was agreed that this system would continue for ten years unless it was ended by mutual consent sooner.
 
• It was also agreed upon to allocate a certain portion of money from the educational grant for the education of the depressed classes in all the provinces.
 
• Nobody would be discriminated against because they belonged to the depressed classes in the matter of election to the local bodies or appointment to government service.

questions.question: In which among the following orbits does the satellites circle Earth directly above the equator?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Geostationary orbit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The satellites that circle Earth directly above the equator are in a Geostationary orbit.
 
• **Geostationary Orbit:**
 
 
• **​**This is a type of geosynchronous orbit, which means the satellite's orbital period is the same as the rotation period of the Earth.
 
 
 
• A satellite in a** Geostationary orbit appears stationary with respect to an observer on the Earth's surface.**
 
• **Location:**
 
 
• **​**Geostationary orbits are directly above the Earth's equator and follow the direction of the Earth's rotation.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• **​**These orbits are particularly useful for communication, weather observation, and other satellites that need a constant view of one area of the surface.
 
 
 
• **Orbit Height:**
 
 
• **​**The geostationary orbit is at an altitude of approximately** 35,786 kilometers (22,236 miles) above Earth's equator.**
 
 
 
• **Satellite Speed:**
 
 
• **​**Satellites in geostationary orbit travel at the same rotational speed as the Earth, which allows them to stay in the same position relative to the Earth's surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d864079bed210be1ba9b6509ff9e5e69d1f49587719b4e0d0618e718d490a79.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Name
 Description
 Notable Information
 
 
 
 

 Sun Orbit
 This is not an orbit around the Earth but around the Sun. Planets, including Earth, follow this path.
 It doesn't apply to satellites orbiting Earth.
 
 

 Low Orbit
 Also known as Low Earth Orbit (LEO), these are satellite systems used in telecommunication, which orbit between 400 and 1,000 miles above the earth's surface.
 Satellites in these orbits move relatively quickly and do not remain fixed over the equator.
 
 

 No Stationary Orbit
 This term does not specifically describe an established class of orbit.
 It might refer to any orbit where the satellite does not remain in a fixed position relative to the Earth's surface.
